hints: First sort out which ring is which in lactose. Compare carbon 4 (the left side of each ring) with the four monomers above, the OH up means galactose and the OH down means glucose.

Now focus on carbon 1, the carbon on the right side of each ring. In the top diagrams beta has the OH pointing up and alpha has the OH pointing down, and in lactose the glycosidic O takes the place of that OH on the left monomer.
walkthrough:
**Tell glucose from galactose using carbon 4**

Look at the left side carbon of each ring. In beta-glucose and alpha-glucose the OH is down (HO below, H above). In beta-galactose and alpha-galactose the OH is up (HO above, H below).

In lactose, the left ring has OH up on the left, so it is galactose. The right ring has OH down on the left, so it is glucose.

**Tell alpha from beta using carbon 1**

Carbon 1 is the anomeric carbon on the right side of each ring. Compare the top four structures. Beta forms have the C1 OH pointing up, alpha forms have the C1 OH pointing down.

This is the key rule for 9700:
$$ \text{beta = OH up, alpha = OH down at C1} $$

**Apply the rule to lactose**

Look at the right ring (glucose) in lactose. Its free C1 on the far right still has OH pointing up, just like beta-glucose. So it is beta-glucose.

Look at the left ring (galactose). Its C1 is now joined in the glycosidic bond, but the bond leaves in the up position, exactly where the OH was in beta-galactose. So it is beta-galactose. Together this gives beta-glucose and beta-galactose.

options.A: Not correct. Neither monomer matches the alpha pattern with C1 OH down, both match the beta up pattern.
options.B: Not correct. The galactose part is beta, but the glucose part on the right also has its C1 OH up, so it is not alpha-glucose.
options.C: Not correct. The glucose part is beta, but the galactose part on the left forms its glycosidic bond in the up beta position, not the alpha down position.
options.D: Correct. The left ring is galactose with the bond in the beta up position, and the right ring is glucose with free C1 OH up, so beta-galactose plus beta-glucose.
